{{short description|Canadian mathematician}}
[[File:Kenneth Davidson.jpg|thumb|Kenneth Davidson]]
'''Kenneth Ralph Davidson''' (born 1951 in [[Edmonton]], [[Alberta]])<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2014/db-award.html|title=Kenneth Davidson to receive 2014 David Borwein Distinguished Career Award|access-date=2014-12-09|archive-date=2014-12-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141209090846/http://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2014/db-award.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> is [[Professor]] of [[Pure Mathematics]] at the [[University of Waterloo]]. He did his undergraduate work at Waterloo and received his Ph.D. under the supervision of [[William Arveson]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1976. Davidson was Director of the [[Fields Institute]] from 2001 to 2004. His areas of research include [[operator theory]] and [[C*-algebra]]s. Since 2007 he has been appointed University Professor at the University of Waterloo.<ref>University Professors at the University of Waterloo http://provost.uwaterloo.ca/universityprofessors.html</ref>

He is a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]].  He was appointed Fellow of the [[Fields Institute]] in 2006. In 2018 the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] listed him in their inaugural class of fellows.<ref>{{citation|url=https://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2018/Fellows|title=Canadian Mathematical Society Inaugural Class of Fellows|publisher=Canadian Mathematical Society|date=December 7, 2018|access-date=January 7, 2020|archive-date=January 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122125232/https://www2.cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2018/Fellows|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Publications==
* ''Real Analysis and Applications'', with Allan Donsig, [[Undergraduate Texts in Mathematics]], Springer, 2009.
* ''<math>C^\ast</math>-Algebras by Example'', Fields Institute Monograph 6, AMS, 1996.
* ''Nest Algebras'', Pitman Research Notes in Math. 191, Longman, 1988.
